segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: What was to follow or to continue, to carry on?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Seguir.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Seguir. And how was I continue, or I carry on, or I follow?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Sigo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Sigo, good. If you want to say I continue speaking, here we use the -ing, I continue speaking. So, how would that be?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Sigo hablando.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Sigo hablando. He continues speaking?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Sigue hablando.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Sigue hablando. He continues speaking, she continues speaking, you formal continue speaking. It's probable that he continues speaking. So in English we would probably say he'll probably continue speaking, but in Spanish, it is probable that he continues speaking. So, how would that be?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Es probable que siga hablando.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Very good. Es probable que siga hablando. Good. It's probable that he continues speaking. So, after seguir to get the meaning of continue, we can use the -ing. What was to be for characteristics?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Ser.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Ser, good. How would you make that -ing form of ser?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Siendo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Siendo. Free, in the sense of not requiring any money, is gratis in Spanish.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Gratis.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: This is where we get gratuitous from in English. It's a bit gratuitous, it's unnecessary, it's free, it's extra, gratis. So you can say it's imperative that it continues to be free. So it's imperative that it continues being free, how would you say that?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Es imperativo que siga siendo gratis.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Es imperativo que siga siendo gratis. To start, we said that we had comenzar and empezar. Comenzar is of course easier to remember and use because it sounds like commence, but empezar is probably more common. So you can use whichever you like now. How would you say, it's spectacular that they start to speak Spanish? Now, after start to connect to the next to-form you need a. There are just a handful of verbs that are not verbs of movement, for example, like ir, volver, salir, that need a to connect. Apart from these, there are just a handful of verbs that use some preposition to connect, and empezar and comenzar are two of them. So, how would you say, it's spectacular that they begin to speak Spanish? Spectacular is the same word in Spanish.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Es espectacular...

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Almost the same word.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Oh, right, espectacular.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Es espectacular that they begin...

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: ...que comiencen a hablar español.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Es espectacular que comiencen a hablar español. It's spectacular that they start to speak Spanish. Now after comenzar and empezar you could also put the -ing form, and the meaning would change a little. It would mean it's spectacular that they start out speaking Spanish. Now in English there's not a lot of difference that they begin to speak Spanish, that they begin speaking Spanish, both in English mean to start speaking Spanish. But in Spanish, if you use the -ing here, it would mean that they start out speaking Spanish, like right from the beginning. So, when I'm speaking about these courses, for example, I say that we start out speaking Spanish right from the beginning. Now speaking about that in Spanish, I would use the -ing here. So, it's spectacular that they start out speaking Spanish.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Es espectacular que comiencen hablando español.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good, and here we don't need the a because we're not connecting to a to-form. What was the verb to finish, or to terminate?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Terminar.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Terminar. Now, if you want to say a sentence like I want you guys to speak with me when you finish selling them, we will say when you finish to sell them. Here we won't use the -ing. But to finish, terminar, is also one of those verbs that needs a preposition to connect to the next to-form. In this case, the preposition is de. So to finish selling them is terminar de vender. So, I want you guys to speak with me when you finish selling them. So the first bit is, I want you guys to speak with me. How is that bit?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Quiero que hablen conmigo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Mood tense. Quiero que hablen conmigo. Good, I want that you talk with me, quiero que hablen conmigo when you finish selling them. So when you finish, and we're still speaking to you guys.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Cuando terminen...

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Why did you use the mood tense there? Cuando terminen?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Because it's it's the future when.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. When cuando refers to generally we won't use the mood tense, we just use the present, and here referring to a future event that hasn't happened, after cuando we use the mood tense, well remembered. Quiero que hablen conmigo cuando terminen when you finish selling them. And we're not going to use selling, we're going to use to sell, and we connect that with de.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: ...cuando terminen de venderlo-s. Venderlos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Venderlos. Good. So all together: I want you guys to speak with me when you finish selling them.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Quiero que hablen conmigo cuando terminen de venderlos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Quiero que hablen conmigo cuando terminen de venderlos. So this means I want you guys to speak with me when you finish selling them. But terminar we can also use like end up. I want you guys to speak with me when you end up selling them. So using the -ing form after terminar instead of de and the to-form gives us this meaning of end up. So if you wanted to say, I want you guys to speak with me when you end up selling them, so I want you guys to speak with me...

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Quiero que hablen conmigo...

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: ...when you end up selling them. So we will say when you finish, and then we will actually use the -ing.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: ...cuando terminen vendiéndolos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Quiero que hablen conmigo cuando terminen vendiéndolos. I want you guys to speak with me when you end up selling them. So, there is a difference here, depending on whether we use the to-form or the -ing form. Just as we saw with empezar or comenzar, there can be a difference between using the to-form afterwards or the -ing form afterwards, and both of them need a preposition to join the to-form, which might be a clue to you that there is a difference between using the to-form and then the -ing form. If the to-form is joining with a preposition, then maybe this particular verb takes the -ing form afterwards as well with a slightly different meaning: empezar a hablar, to start to speak, to start speaking; empezar hablando, to actually begin something speaking, or as we would probably say, to start out speaking; terminar de vender, to finish selling; terminar vendiendo, to end up selling. So what we have aimed to teach here is the idea of the mood tense, the general feeling of the mood tense, and the kind of constructions in which it occurs. And like I said, understanding the mood tense is about listening out for it and listening out for how people around you use it. A great way to learn it is to chat online, for example, because maybe in real life, and almost certainly at the beginning, you won't pick up those subtle changes in vowels that you get with the mood tense. But if you're chatting online, you will notice quite clearly, "Ah, oh, there they used an A and not an E. Oh, there they used an E and not an A. Oh, why?" And then you will look at the context of the sentence and work out why the mood tense was used, and that really is the best way to internalize it.
